reasoning: Unlike the rectangular cuts in N340542, the bulk U.S.-origin polycarbonate sheet is routed to a specific custom contour and edge-bent in Canada to fit the angle of a Tesla Model Y glass roof, plus combined with Chinese nano tape. Similar to N357927 (machining raw sheets into a dedicated article in Canada), this custom shaping and forming transforms the raw sheet into a new automotive accessory, conferring Canadian origin.

key_factors: 19 CFR 102.11(b)(1) / substantial transformation (essential character of the oil)
decisive_step: Harvesting ahiflower seeds and cold-pressing into crude ahiflower oil in the United Kingdom
flip: If the ahiflower seeds were imported into Canada and pressed into oil in Canada (as in N351895 and N352583), the origin would be Canada.
reasoning: Crude ahiflower oil and refined ahiflower oil are both classified under heading 1515, HTSUS. Under USMCA marking rules (19 CFR 102.11(a)(3)), refining crude oil in Canada fails the 19 CFR 102.20 tariff shift rule (which requires a shift from another chapter). Under 19 CFR 102.11(b)(1) and traditional substantial transformation analysis, the single material that imparts the essential character is the crude ahiflower oil (99.9%) produced in the United Kingdom; refining merely purifies the existing oil without changing its fundamental character.

decisive_step: Fabrication of dedicated steel cabinet components (plates, panels, upright columns) in Thailand
flip: Forming and stamping the steel panels, plates, and columns from raw steel sheet in the United States prior to welding
reasoning: All essential structural components (top/base plates, 6 side panels, 2 upright columns) are pre-fabricated in Thailand, already having the essential character of an unassembled cabinet (GRI 2(a)) or dedicated parts under heading 9403. Under 19 CFR 102.20(r) for heading 9403 (and substantial transformation principles), assembly of pre-made furniture parts into a finished cabinet in the U.S. via welding, grinding, and painting does not satisfy the required tariff shift or transform the Thai-origin components into a product of the U.S.

decisive_step: Molding, forming, and assembly of the lure bodies and flashers in Canada
flip: Forming the lure bodies and flasher blades in another country prior to simple assembly in Canada
reasoning: Fishing lures and flashers of heading 9507 are non-textile goods, though under the 19 CFR Part 102 hierarchy (analogous to 102.21(c)(2)/(c)(4) and USMCA marking rules in 102.11), origin is conferred where the foreign components undergo the required tariff shift or where the lure body/blade (which imparts essential character per GRI 3(b) and HQ 951921) is formed and assembled. Because this is a USMCA fishing tackle ruling (typically Canadian tackle such as Hot Spot/Scotty/Tomic lures), manufacturing the bodies in Canada confers Canadian origin.

decisive_step: Assembly and machining of the turbocharger kit at BD Engine Brake Inc. in Canada
flip: Performing final assembly and testing of the turbocharger in the country where the housings and wheels were cast
reasoning: Although 19 CFR 102.21 applies to textiles, under 19 CFR 102.11/substantial transformation (and by analogy 102.21(c)(2)/(c)(4)), the essential character of the BD Diesel Turbo Thruster II Kit (heading 8414) is imparted by the turbocharger assembly. Consistent with N359690 and N341003, BD Engine Brake Inc. (a Canadian manufacturer) machines and assembles the complex components (compressor/turbine wheels, housings, wastegate actuator) into a complete, calibrated turbocharger in Canada, conferring Canadian origin.

decisive_step: Reclamation of lead and plastic from scrap, fabrication of lead plates and molded cases, and complete battery assembly in Mexico
flip: If the lead plates and battery cases were fabricated in another country (e.g., Thailand) and only underwent simple final assembly in Mexico
reasoning: In Mexico, U.S. scrap batteries are crushed, separated, smelted into lead ingots, fabricated into lead plates, and molded into plastic cases and covers, which are then assembled with foreign and domestic components into new lead-acid automotive batteries. Under CBP origin rules (both 19 CFR 102.20 tariff shift for heading 8507 and substantial transformation, as seen in N330771 and N341165, and analogous to 102.21(c)(2)), the processing and full assembly in Mexico confer Mexican origin.

decisive_step: Controlled mixing of bulk glues of different viscosities and retail packaging in Mexico, shifting classification from subheading 3506.99 to 3506.10
flip: If the glues were imported into Mexico already at the final viscosity and only repackaged into smaller bottles without controlled blending, or if the bulk glues were already classified under subheading 3506.10, the country of origin would remain Taiwan.
reasoning: The bulk glues from Taiwan (subheading 3506.99) undergo controlled blending of varying viscosities and retail packaging in Mexico to create manicure glues classified under subheading 3506.10.5000. Under 19 CFR 102.11(a)(3) and 102.20 (analogous to 102.21(c)(2)), as well as GN 11(o) Chapter 35 Rule 4(A), a tariff shift to subheading 3506.10 from any other subheading (including 3506.99) is satisfied in Mexico, conferring Mexican origin.

decisive_step: All raw materials, fabric formation, batting production, cutting, quilting, and sewing occur in China
flip: Form the outer woven fabrics and batting, and perform the quilting and assembly, in a second country such as Thailand (similar to N357875).
reasoning: Every single production step—from growing cotton and extruding polyester yarn to weaving the outer fabrics, producing the nonwoven batting, cutting, quilting, and binding—takes place entirely within China. Because the moving blanket is wholly obtained or produced in a single country, its country of origin is China pursuant to 19 CFR 102.21(c)(1).

decisive_step: formation of the polyester woven fabric for the roof and walls in China
flip: Weaving the polyester roof and wall fabric in South Korea would shift origin to South Korea under (c)(2).
reasoning: The sun shelter is classified as a tent under heading 6306. It is not wholly obtained in one country ((c)(1)). Under (c)(2), the 102.21(e) rule for 6306 requires fabric formation in a single country, which fails because fabrics are formed in both China and South Korea. Heading 6306 is excluded from the wholly assembled rule in (c)(3)(ii). Under (c)(4), consistent with N336815 and N352382, the most important manufacturing process is the formation of the outer shell (roof/walls) fabric in China.

key_factors: (c)(5) last country of important manufacturing or assembly process
decisive_step: Knitting the micro mink fabric and cutting and sewing the fabrics into the finished throw in Vietnam
flip: Knit the polyester micro mink backing fabric in China instead of Vietnam
reasoning: The throw blanket is classified under heading 6301. Under 19 CFR 102.21(c)(1)-(2), origin is not conferred because the two fabrics are knit in different countries (China and Vietnam). Heading 6301 is excluded from (c)(3)(ii). Under (c)(4), neither the face nor backing fabric formation alone is the single most important manufacturing process. Therefore, under 19 CFR 102.21(c)(5), origin is Vietnam, the last country where important manufacturing (knitting the backing fabric) and assembly occurred, matching precedent N358231 and N348569.

decisive_step: Forming the molded polycarbonate shells and assembling the suitcases in Mexico (Scenarios 1-3)
flip: Molding the rigid polycarbonate outer shells in China prior to shipping them to Mexico for simple final assembly (as in Scenario 4) shifts the origin to China.
reasoning: The suitcases are classified in subheading 4202.12.21, HTSUS (outer surface of plastics, not subject to 19 CFR 102.21 textile rules). For USMCA marking under 19 CFR 102.11(a)(3) and substantial transformation, a shift to 4202.12 from any other chapter is satisfied in Mexico in Scenarios 1-3 where the rigid polycarbonate shells (which impart the essential character) are formed and assembled. In Scenario 4, because the pre-formed shells and all other components originate in China, assembly in Mexico does not confer origin.

key_factors: (c)(4) most important assembly or manufacturing process
decisive_step: Formation of the meltblown nonwoven filtration fabric layer in the United States
flip: Forming the meltblown nonwoven fabric layer in China or Mexico instead of the United States
reasoning: The laminated nonwoven fabric (heading 5603) is not wholly obtained in one country ((c)(1)). Under (c)(2), heading 5603 requires a shift from fibers; since the two nonwoven layers are formed in the U.S. and China and merely laminated in Mexico, no single country meets the tariff shift. Heading 5603 is excluded from (c)(3)(ii). Under (c)(4), fabric formation is the most important manufacturing process. The U.S.-formed meltblown layer provides the primary filtration function, making its formation in the U.S. decisive.

decisive_step: Fabrication, sub-assembly, and final integration/assembly of the mechanical and electrical components in Canada
flip: If the pump, motor, brush assembly, and main housing were pre-assembled in a foreign country and only packaged in Canada, origin would be that foreign country.
reasoning: Although 19 CFR 102.21 applies to textiles, under analogous rules (19 CFR 102.21(c)(2)/(c)(3)) and the substantial transformation test (as applied in H332525 and N359690), the SkyOiler 360 (HTSUS 8479.89.9599) undergoes its decisive manufacturing and assembly in Canada. In Canada, the mounting bracket assemblies are fabricated, the brush systems are cut and assembled, and the pump, motor, electrical components, and housing are fully integrated and tested to create a new article with a distinct name, character, and use.

decisive_step: Fabrication of the steel mop frame and hitch system and final assembly of the complete mop unit in Canada
flip: Fabricate the steel frame and hitch system and perform final assembly of the mop unit in the United States instead of Canada
reasoning: The TigerMop is classified under subheading 9603.90.8050, HTSUS (a non-102.21 heading; under USMCA marking rules in 19 CFR 102.11(a)(3) and 102.20, heading 9603 requires a change to heading 9603 from any other chapter). Although the textile mop head is assembled in the US from Vietnamese materials and shipped to Canada, the steel mop frame and hitch system are fabricated in Canada from foreign materials, and all components undergo final assembly into the complete article in Canada, conferring Canadian origin.

key_factors: (c)(2) tariff shift / lamination of face veneer
decisive_step: Bonding the face veneer to the core and profiling into multilayer wood flooring panels in Canada
flip: Bonding the face veneer to the core substrate in the country where the substrate was manufactured prior to export to Canada.
reasoning: Following CBP precedents N335201 and N339851 on multilayer wood flooring of heading 4412, the country of origin is conferred where the face veneer is laminated/bonded to the wood core substrate and profiled with tongue-and-groove edges (Canada), as this assembly creates the multilayer flooring panel and imparts its essential character.

decisive_step: Spreading, resin impregnation, and thermal bonding of UHMWPE filaments into nonwoven fabric in South Korea
flip: Forming the nonwoven fabric webs in China prior to shipping them to South Korea for mere lamination.
reasoning: Both composite articles are nonwoven fabrics of heading 5603 (over 90% textile filament by weight, laminated with plastic film not visible/predominant under Chapter 56/59 notes). Under 19 CFR 102.21(c)(1), the goods are not wholly obtained in a single country due to Chinese inputs. Under 19 CFR 102.21(c)(2) and 102.21(e)(1) for heading 5603, foreign materials from headings 5402 and 3920 undergo the required tariff shift (a change to heading 5603 from any other heading, except 5601-5602) when the nonwoven fabric is formed in South Korea across all scenarios.

key_factors: Substantial transformation (rough hub casting predetermined to final shape/use)
decisive_step: Casting of the rough brake hub in China
flip: Cast the rough brake hubs in Mexico instead of importing them from China.
reasoning: Under CBP substantial transformation precedent for automotive hub and brake components (and analogous to N336333 and N336183), a rough hub casting imported from China already possesses the predetermined shape, form, and essential character of the finished hub. Machining (CNC turning, drilling, tapping, countersinking) and pressing/coupling bearing cups, studs, tone rings, and Mexican brake drums in Mexico are finishing and simple assembly operations that do not substantially transform the Chinese hub, so China remains the country of origin.

decisive_step: Weaving of the polypropylene webbed fabric in Cambodia
flip: Weaving the polypropylene webbed fabric in China instead of Cambodia.
reasoning: The lashing strap is an other made-up textile article classified under heading 6307, HTSUS. Because it is produced in both China and Cambodia, 19 CFR 102.21(c)(1) does not apply. Under 19 CFR 102.21(c)(2) and the tariff shift rule in 102.21(e) for heading 6307 (as seen in N334983 and N347100), origin is conferred by the single country where the fabric is formed by a fabric-making process. Since the polypropylene webbed fabric is woven in Cambodia, the country of origin is Cambodia.

decisive_step: Cutting of fabrics into panels and complete assembly of the cap in the Dominican Republic
flip: Perform part of the sewing/assembly of the crown panels or peak in Vietnam or South Korea prior to shipping to the Dominican Republic
reasoning: The baseball-style cap is classified under heading 6505, HTSUS, and is not wholly obtained in a single country under 19 CFR 102.21(c)(1). Under 102.21(c)(2) and 102.21(e), for non-knit-to-shape headgear of heading 6505, the required tariff shift is to heading 6505 from any other heading, except from heading 6507, provided the good is wholly assembled in a single country. Because the snapback closure is classified outside 6507 and the cap is wholly assembled in the Dominican Republic, the Dominican Republic confers origin.

key_factors: (c)(2) tariff shift and substantial transformation via fabrication and assembly
decisive_step: Cutting, bending, hole punching, welding, galvanizing, powder coating, and final assembly of the steel tubes into the safety gate in Mexico
flip: Importing pre-welded, pre-shaped gate frames from China and performing only minor assembly of the plastic locks and end caps in Mexico
reasoning: Chinese raw steel tubes, plastic parts, and fasteners are shipped to Mexico where the tubes undergo extensive fabrication (cutting, bending, punching, welding, galvanizing, and powder coating) and final assembly into a household steel safety gate (heading 7323). This processing satisfies the required tariff shift and constitutes a substantial transformation of all foreign materials in a single country, conferring Mexican origin (consistent with the fabrication principles in N359668 and N357851).

decisive_step: Knitting and weaving of the polyester fabrics in China
flip: Forming the textile fabrics (plush knit, ribbed corduroy woven, and nonwoven) in Indonesia rather than China
reasoning: Textile pet toys are classified as other made-up textile articles under subheading 6307.90.9891, HTSUS. Under 19 CFR 102.21(c)(1), the toys are not wholly obtained in a single country. Under 102.21(c)(2) and the tariff shift rule in 102.21(e)(1) for heading 6307, origin is conferred by the country where the fabric is formed by a fabric-making process (consistent with N348140 and N349766). Because all fabrics for both toys are knitted, woven, or formed in China, the country of origin is China.

decisive_step: Braiding of the filament yarns into rope in Slovakia
flip: Braiding the rope in China before shipping to Slovakia for coating and cutting
reasoning: The braided synthetic rope is classified under heading 5607, HTSUS (or heading 5609 if imported cut to length with spliced ends). It is not wholly obtained in a single country under 19 CFR 102.21(c)(1). Under 19 CFR 102.21(c)(2) and the tariff shift rules in 102.21(e)(1) for headings 5607 and 5609, origin is conferred by a change from any other heading, including filament yarn of heading 5402. Because the Chinese 5402 filament yarn is braided into rope in Slovakia, the tariff shift occurs in Slovakia.

decisive_step: Injection molding and assembly of plastic resin into containers in Canada
flip: If the containers were injection molded in the United States and only inspected and packaged in Canada, the country of origin would be the United States.
reasoning: The plastic archival containers are classified in subheading 3926.90.9989, HTSUS. Because they are made in Canada from U.S.-origin polypropylene resin, they are not wholly obtained in a single country. Under the Part 102 rules (19 CFR 102.11(a)(3) and 102.20, analogous to 102.21(c)(2)), the rule for heading 3926 requires a change to headings 3922-3926 from any other subheading (see N357063 and N352810). The U.S. resin (heading 3902) undergoes the required tariff shift via injection molding in Canada, conferring Canadian origin.

decisive_step: Manufacturing and injection overmolding assembly in Mexico
flip: If the steel pin, bushing, and locking ring were imported already assembled from China and only packaged in Mexico, origin would be China.
reasoning: Although the prompt references 19 CFR 102.21, a steel/plastic container bolt seal is a non-textile composite article of heading 7326/8309 evaluated for USMCA marking under 19 CFR 102.11 (as in N364328 and N343893). Based on the USMCA inquiry context and analogous Mexican manufacturing rulings (N364328), forming/machining components and overmolding the plastic lock body onto the steel components in Mexico satisfies the 19 CFR 102.11(a)(3) / (c)(2) tariff shift, conferring Mexican origin.

decisive_step: Braiding and assembly of the rope in Slovakia
flip: If the HMPE filament yarns were braided into the rope in China instead of Slovakia, the origin would be China.
reasoning: The braided synthetic rope is classified under heading 5607 (or 5609 if fitted with spliced terminations). Under 19 CFR 102.21(c)(1), the rope is not wholly obtained in a single country. Under 19 CFR 102.21(c)(2), the tariff shift rule in 102.21(e) for heading 5607 (and 5609) requires a change from any other heading, except from yarn of 5004-5006, 5106-5110, 5204-5207, 5306-5308, or 5401-5511. However, if the good is of continuous filaments, a change to 5607 from filament yarns of 5402 is permitted if the braiding/twisting into cordage occurs in a single country, or under (c)(3)/(c)(4) the whole assembly and braiding of the load-bearing core and cover occurs in Slovakia.

key_factors: (c)(2) tariff shift / (c)(4) most important manufacturing process
decisive_step: Manufacturing of the hopper cone bottom with integrated aeration plenums and packaging with the U.S. upper bin in Canada
flip: Manufacturing the hopper cone bottom in the United States instead of Canada
reasoning: The grain hopper bin with aeration system is classified as a storage unit fitted with mechanical/thermal equipment (heading 8479 or 7309). Because the U.S. upper bin and Canadian hopper cone bottom with built-in aeration plenums are combined in Canada as a single functional system, and the Canadian cone provides the critical aeration/discharge mechanism (or under 19 CFR 102.19 NAFTA/USMCA marking override where U.S./Canadian inputs are combined in Canada), the country of origin is Canada.

decisive_step: Weaving of the cotton fabric and formation of batting and scrim in Vietnam
flip: Weaving the cotton greige fabric in China instead of Vietnam
reasoning: The quilt (heading 9404) and sham (heading 9404 or 6304) are not wholly obtained in a single country under (c)(1) due to processing in China. Under 19 CFR 102.21(c)(2) and (e)(1), goods of 9404.90 and 6304 without embroidery, lace, braid, edging, trimming, piping, or applique work originate where the fabric is formed by a fabric-making process. All fabrics (cotton woven fabric, polyester batting, olefin scrim) are formed in Vietnam. Printing/bleaching in China is a non-origin-conferring finishing step (cf. N349998).
